teams.heading: Jake White names Nathan Hughes in Fiji squad with four uncapped players
teams.body: Former England international Nathan Hughes is back in Fiji's frame, drafted into Jake White's 35-man extended squad for the Nations Championship after winning 22 England caps between 2016 and 2019. White has also named four uncapped players, and could hand Peniami Narisia, Marika Parker and Setareki Bituniyata their first Test caps this month. Ben Volavola keeps his place after ending a three-year wait for a Test cap against Japan last weekend, as Fiji look to climb off the bottom of the Southern Hemisphere pool.

lead.why: Fiji's own squad news, with a returning former England international and four uncapped players, and it hasn't been covered in the earlier editions.

teams.heading: Blamire and Oghre shine in PREM clash amid Tuipulotu injury concern
teams.body: Leicester's 22-16 bonus-point win at Bristol on Friday night in the PREM gave England's hooker hopefuls a showcase at Ashton Gate. Jamie Blamire, who scored for Leicester, and Gabe Oghre both starred in a set-piece battle, and Planet Rugby reckons both men "nailed their final audition" for next week's England training squad. Their showing came amid an injury concern to Kepu Tuipulotu ahead of the Nations Championship.

lead.why: The only England-linked men's story in the pack with a national-team hook, covering two hookers pushing for the England training squad.

teams.heading: Jamie Benson recalls shock of Andy Farrell's July call before joining Ulster
teams.body: Jamie Benson has described a swift rise that began with a surprise call from Andy Farrell. The 24-year-old, then at Harlequins and already in an England A squad, was summoned to Ireland training in July before he had even joined Ulster. "Obviously, it was a bit of a shock to be called in here before I'd even set foot in Ulster, but it was a great feeling," he says. The versatile back has impressed for Ulster and is now in the Ireland squad for the Nations Championship campaign.

lead.why: A fresh first-person interview with an uncapped squad newcomer, with direct quotes, is the most shareable new Ireland item in the pack.

teams.heading: Italy U18 beat Ireland 36-29 in Badia Polesine after trailing at half-time
teams.body: Italy U18 opened their season on Saturday with a 36-29 win over Ireland in Badia Polesine, matching last year's success in Cosenza. Ireland led 17-12 at half-time, despite Italy losing two players to yellow cards, the second for Nikitakos at 36 minutes, but the Azzurrini changed gear after the interval. Fanzo and Agressi scored second-half tries, with Vaccaretti converting both, and captain Mesaglio's try had opened the scoring for Italy.

lead.why: The only new item in the pack, and it is a result for an Italy side, so it is the freshest story available.

teams.heading: Fergus Watson opens scoring as Glasgow Warriors beat Lions 28-20
teams.body: Scotland's Glasgow Warriors beat the Lions 28-20 in the United Rugby Championship at Scotstoun, keeping their unbeaten run alive. Fergus Watson, Player of the Match, scored the opening try off a Dan Lancaster cross-kick, and Lancaster added the second before the half-hour as the hosts led 19-3 at the break. The Lions fought back through Morne van den Berg and Morne Brandon, but Ollie Smith scored late for the hosts and a George Horne penalty denied the visitors a bonus point.

lead.why: A fresh report on Glasgow's URC win that is not the Singleton debut story already run, and it names the Scottish club in its opening sentence.

teams.heading: Carwyn Leggatt-Jones rated 7 as Scarlets fall 54-26 to Bulls in Pretoria
teams.body: Scarlets fly-half Carwyn Leggatt-Jones earned a 7 in WalesOnline's ratings of the 54-26 defeat at the Bulls in Pretoria, where the Scarlets threatened to shock the Bulls before falling away late on. The verdict: 'Another assured performance by the young fly-half. Never hides away in attack.' WalesOnline's headline links the Scarlets showing to Wales coaches' interest, and the ratings also credit Corey Domachowski for managing 52 minutes on his return from injury.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the pack with substantive reporting, and it puts a Welsh club player's form in front of Wales coaches' attention.

teams.heading: Facundo Isa recalled to Argentina squad for Ireland, replacing injured Santiago Grondona
teams.body: Veteran Facundo Isa is back in the Argentina squad for Ireland, named in place of the injured Santiago Grondona in Contepomi's finalised 33-man roster. Isa had missed out on international duty in 2024 and 2026, and his only Argentina outing in that time came in July 2025. The recall comes amid a run of withdrawals: Thomas Gallo and Santiago Carreras were ruled out after being named, while Ignacio Ruiz and Joaquín Oviedo are also unavailable.

lead.why: A fresh selection call for the Ireland test that the Sunday briefing has not yet covered, and it names a returning veteran.

teams.heading: England's Fin Smith calf injury clouds Wallabies' Nations Championship opener
teams.body: England are fretting over Fin Smith's fitness before the Nations Championship opener against Australia. Smith damaged a calf against Leicester and cannot join the three-day camp in Bagshot. The 24-year-old started at 10 in all three of England's July Tests. With limited preparation time, there will inevitably be disruption to Steve Borthwick's plans. Gloucester's Charlie Atkinson has been called up as cover, with Marcus Smith and George Ford also in the squad. England's management say they remain hopeful Smith will be back in time to face the Wallabies.

teams.heading: Leicester Fainga'anuku's hybrid role gives Rennie bench versatility, Stephen Donald says
teams.body: Leicester Fainga'anuku, named in the All Blacks squad for the November matches after missing the July games, could give Dave Rennie a bench with real range. Stephen Donald, speaking on The Aftermatch with Kirst and Beav, said a player who covers both loose forward and back positions could let New Zealand carry two loosies and still keep a flexible reserve. "It gives them real freedom up front to have more impact in those ball-carrying loose forward positions," he said. Rennie names his team for the first Test next week.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist about the All Blacks themselves, and it covers a selection question fans will argue about.

teams.heading: Marcell Coetzee scores twice as Bulls thrash Scarlets 54-26 in Pretoria
teams.body: Marcell Coetzee came off the bench to score twice as the Bulls beat the Scarlets 54-26 in Pretoria on Saturday, moving them into second place before the Nations Championship break. The 35-year-old replaced Cameron Hanekom early in the second half and provided the composure the Bulls needed after the Scarlets had levelled at 26-26 from 19-0 down. Grobbelaar and De Klerk also scored from the bench, and the Bulls put 28 unanswered points on the Scarlets in the final quarter.

lead.why: Coetzee's two tries and the Bulls bench give a fresh South Africa performance story that is not covered by the Furlong or Hansen pieces already reported.
